newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. said to offer France crisis force role -paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. said to offer France crisis force role -paper.

text.p: The United States has offered a compromise in a dispute with France over NATO's southern command, under which the French might lead a new southern crisis force, the International Herald Tribune (IHT) said on Friday.

The Paris-based newspaper quoted unidentified U.S. officials as saying the offer was part of an effort to persuade France to drop its threat to halt further integration into NATO's military structure unless Washington yields the key southern regional command in Naples to a European.
The southern command controls the Mediterranean and has always been headed by an American admiral, who also commands the U.S. Sixth Fleet.
The U.S. embassy declined comment on the newspaper report. French officials said it might be a trial balloon floated to test Paris' reaction.
French Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said Franco-American talks were making progress and must be settled before a NATO summit in Madrid in July "on the basis of parity and balance".
"We have good hope that we will be able to achieve a satisfactory solution on that basis when the time comes," he said.

The IHT said the proposed new rapid-reaction force, a step down in the hierarchy from the regional headquarters in Naples, would probably be based in Florence and focus primarily on potential crises in the western Mediterranean.
That would leave bigger threats in the east Mediterranean involving the Balkans, the Middle East or the Gulf, to the U.S.-led southern command.
Italy reported last week that European allies had discussed a compromise proposal under which NATO would agree to review the issue of the southern command in five or six years' time.
But diplomats said France had rejected that idea as insufficient, demanding an immediate sharing of responsibilities on an equal level between Americans and Europeans.
